data.title: ADR-002: JSON as the format of a journal event
body: # ADR-002: JSON as the format of a journal event
- **Status:** accepted
- **Scope:** architecture
## Context
The spike of 2026-09-02 (PRD, section 6.4) showed that reading 10 000 events takes **0.43 s** — twice the 200 ms guardrail. Events in the spike were stored in YAML.
It had to be established what exactly was the cause: the number of files, the filesystem, or the parser.
Measured on those same 10 000 events:
| Format | Parsing 10k events | Bytes per event |
| JSON (`JSON.parse`) | **6 ms** | 174 |
The difference is **83×**. That is, almost all the time measured in the spike was not I/O but the YAML parser.
## Alternatives considered
| Option | Pros | Cons |
| JSON | Native parser, 83× faster; zero dependencies; `JSON.parse` does not execute code | 24 bytes more per event; quoted keys read slightly worse to the eye |
| YAML | Pleasanter for a human; smaller volume | 496 ms for 10k events exceeds the whole CLI budget on its own; pulls in a dependency of 686 KB |
| JSONL (a line = an event) | Compact, fast | Returns to a shared file, and that is 2 conflicts out of 3 by the spike's measurements — it contradicts the product's main hypothesis |
| MessagePack and other binary formats | Fastest and most compact | Kills `git diff` as a human-readable journal — and that is the product's main advantage |
## Decision
**JSON, one object per file, without indentation** (`JSON.stringify` without `space`).

The readability argument, which usually plays in YAML's favour, hardly matters here: an event has 7 fields and is shown to the user through `kadence log`, not read from the file by eye. Where readability is genuinely needed — in task descriptions — Markdown with frontmatter remains (ADR-005).
## Consequences
- Positive: an 83-fold speedup of parsing for zero lines of code; one dependency fewer; `git diff` on single-line JSON shows the change as a whole event rather than as a set of lines.
- Cost of the decision: +14% to the size of the journal; `cat` on an event file is less pleasant than it could be.

- What will have to be reconsidered: if events ever grow into nested structures with dozens of fields, single-line JSON will become unreadable in a diff — then it is worth moving to indented JSON, not to YAML.
